# The package

<!-- GENERATED by `scripts/gen-consumer-skills.mjs` — do not edit. Regenerate: `npm run consumer:gen` -->

**This file never names the kit.** Take the real package name from the
consuming project's own `package.json` — it is the dependency whose `exports`
include `./button`. Examples in the skills say `<pkg>` for the same reason:
the kit can be renamed by whoever owns it, and a name written down here would
go quietly out of date.

| | |
| --- | --- |
| Runtime dependencies | **none** — installing the kit adds nothing transitively |
| Module format | ESM and CJS, with types for both |

## Peer dependencies

| Package | Range | Required |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `react` | `^18 || ^19` | yes |
| `react-dom` | `^18 || ^19` | yes |
| `react-hook-form` | `^7` | no — only if the app imports `<pkg>/form` |

Nothing else. The kit has no runtime dependencies, and no dev-only
companion package either: the primitives it is built on are compiled into
`dist`, and their type declarations are inlined into the shipped `.d.ts`,
so `node_modules/<pkg>` is the whole install.

## Stylesheet — pick one route

**The app has no Tailwind.** Import the compiled stylesheet once, at the app
entry. It is self-contained.

```ts
import '<pkg>/styles.css';
```

**The app already runs Tailwind v4.** Take the tokens instead and let the
app's own build generate the utilities:

```css
@import 'tailwindcss';
@import 'tw-animate-css';
@import '<pkg>/tokens.css';
@import '<pkg>/theme.css';

@source '../node_modules/<pkg>/dist';

@custom-variant dark (&:is(.dark *));

@layer base {
  * {
    @apply border-border outline-ring/50;
  }
}
```

Every line of that is load-bearing, and each one fails **silently** — nothing
errors, the page just looks subtly wrong. The compiled stylesheet carries all
of them; this route has to declare them:

| Line | Missing it means |
| --- | --- |
| `@source` | Tailwind never sees the kit's class names and every component renders unstyled |
| `@layer base { * … }` | Tailwind v4 defaults `border-color` to `currentColor`, and the kit draws its rules with a bare `border` / `border-b` — so every table rule, card edge and separator is painted in the **text** colour |
| `@custom-variant dark` | dark mode here is class-driven, but Tailwind's own `dark:` variant defaults to `prefers-color-scheme`, so the kit's internal `dark:` utilities follow the OS instead of the class |
| `tw-animate-css` | `animate-in`, `fade-in-0`, `zoom-in-95` match no rule and the overlays appear with no motion. CSS-only dev dependency: `npm i -D tw-animate-css` |

Do **not** do both routes. Two copies of the same layer is wasted bytes at
best and a specificity fight at worst.

## Import subpaths

50 in total. Import from the subpath, not the barrel — the barrel reaches
every component in the kit.

```ts
import { Button } from '<pkg>/button';        // ✔ Button and its dependencies
import { Button } from '<pkg>';               // ✘ pulls the whole kit
```
